description: Controlled check of WHY masked vs unmasked differs so much more in v4 than v3. In v3 the unmasked baseline was reward-shaped to avoid illegal actions (graded -2..-20 penalties); v4's default reward is not. We retrained the v4 unmasked agent WITH a v3-style illegal-action penalty (-10) to test whether the v4 masking gap is just an unfair baseline or a real environment effect.
conclusion: Teaching the unmasked agent to avoid illegal actions (the v3 approach) barely helped: illegal-rate fell only 87.5->82.2% and success rose only 47.9->54.7%, still far below masked (96.1%). The v3->v4 masking difference is therefore NOT mainly the reward-shaping methodology. It is the ENVIRONMENT: in v3 legality is a stable function of state (learnable, ~5% illegal, ~100% success); in v4 legality is episode-dependent (per-episode scenario randomization), which the unmasked agent cannot reliably infer even when explicitly penalised. Masking supplies the episode-specific legal set structurally, which is why it becomes performance-critical at v4 scale. This is a capability limit, not a motivation limit.
